meta.title: The Most Dangerous Border on Earth Became a Wildlife Sanctuary
meta._convention: One scene-spec JSON per script, saved alongside it as <script-name>.scenes.json. Each beat's `duration` is intentionally omitted here -- build_video.js fills it in at render time from the ACTUAL measured length of that beat's generated narration WAV. North Korea (KP) and South Korea (KR) are both real countries in maps/country-codes.json and use the standard `highlight` convention; the DMZ strip itself is a hand-drawn `lines` band (not a country) following the real MDL's approximate path coast to coast, per the 'scenes that aren't a country' convention.

beats.voText: This is the most heavily fortified border in the world, millions of landmines, guard posts every few hundred meters, soldiers on permanent alert.
beats.onScreenText: The most fortified border on Earth.

beats.voText: It's the Korean DMZ, a 160-mile-long strip separating North and South Korea, created by the 1953 armistice that paused, but never ended, the war.
It's only about 2.5 miles wide, but it's arguably the single most dangerous strip of land on the planet, sealed off from almost all human contact.
And because almost no human has set foot inside since 1953, it's quietly become one of the richest wildlife habitats left in Asia.
beats.onScreenText: No people. So wildlife moved in.

beats.voText: Endangered red-crowned cranes winter here every year, and some researchers believe a species as rare as the Amur leopard may still survive inside.
The most dangerous 2.5 miles on the planet turned out to be one of its most untouched. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
